findings.title: Authorization check uses AND instead of OR for team admin/owner
findings.body: The condition `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires the user to be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner simultaneously. This is almost certainly a logic error — the intent is to allow access if the user is either a team admin OR a team owner. As written, team admins who are not owners (and vice versa) will be incorrectly denied access with a FORBIDDEN error. The operator should be `||`.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives unfiltered `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: On line 168, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original input `guests` array, which may include emails that were filtered out on lines 74-78 (already-existing attendees or blacklisted emails). Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `newGuests` parameter is used to decide whether an attendee receives a full 'AttendeeScheduledEmail' (for new guests) or an 'AttendeeAddGuestsEmail' (for existing attendees). If a pre-existing attendee's email is still in `guests`, they will incorrectly receive the 'you have been scheduled' email instead of the 'new guests were added' notification. The call should pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

findings.title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive for guest emails but blacklist is lowercased
findings.body: The `blacklistedGuestEmails` array is lowercased (line 71), but the incoming `guest` email addresses are compared without lowercasing. A guest email like `Blocked@Example.com` would not match `blocked@example.com` in the blacklist, allowing blacklisted emails to bypass the restriction. The comparison should lowercase the guest email: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())`.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails does not respect eventType email disable settings
findings.body: Unlike other email-sending functions in this file (e.g., `sendLocationChangeEmails`, `sendScheduledEmails`), `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept or check `eventTypeMetadata` for `disableStandardEmails`. This means organizer and attendee emails will be sent even when the event type has explicitly disabled them, violating the user's configuration.

findings.title: Any attendee can add guests to a booking without further authorization
findings.body: The `isAttendee` check on line 52 allows any booking attendee to add arbitrary guests. Depending on the product intent, this may be too permissive — for example, in a team booking scenario, a single attendee could add unlimited external guests. Consider whether this should be restricted to organizers or team admins only, or at least documented as intentional.

findings.title: No rollback if calendar update fails after attendees are persisted
findings.body: The attendees are written to the database on line 92 via `prisma.booking.update`, but the subsequent `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` call on line 165 can fail independently. If it does, the database will have the new attendees but external calendars (Google Calendar, etc.) will not be updated, leading to data inconsistency. There is no compensating transaction or retry mechanism.

findings.title: Hardcoded English string in Tooltip instead of using i18n
findings.body: The Tooltip content `"Remove email"` on line 46 is a hardcoded English string. It should use the `t()` translation function (e.g., `t("remove_email")`) to support internationalization, consistent with the rest of the component which uses `useLocale`.

findings.title: No upper bound on the number of guests that can be added
findings.body: The `guests` array in the input schema has no `.max()` constraint. A malicious or buggy client could submit thousands of email addresses in a single request, causing excessive database writes, email sends, and calendar API calls. Adding a reasonable `.max(N)` limit would mitigate this.
